solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Faction involved in exploit did a runner (8)

indicators.note: the faction is wrapped up inside the exploit

blocks.note: an exploit is a deed; it opens around the camp
a camp is a faction within a group

explanation.surface: A splinter group, caught up in some daring escapade, bolts.
explanation.walkthrough: To do a runner is British slang for leaving in a hurry, often without paying.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly, which is doing a runner.

clue.text: Get rid of fish and gyoza? (8)

blocks.note: to dump is to get rid of
the ling is a long cod-like fish

explanation.surface: A cook throws out the fish and the Japanese dumplings too.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: gyoza are one kind of dumpling.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyoza are Japanese filled dumplings, so a gyoza is a dumpling.

clue.text: Funny pear with bottom sliced off (5)

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom of a word is its last letter, cut away

blocks.note: the Comice is a variety of pear
COMICE loses its final E

explanation.surface: A pear looks silly once its base has been cut away.
explanation.walkthrough: You need to know the pear variety Comice; slicing is apt for fruit and hides the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain adjective synonym: both describe whatever makes people laugh.

clue.text: Unremarkable, misguided hero faded, I’m told (6-2-3-4)

indicators.note: letters that are misguided have been sent the wrong way, so rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, all fifteen letters

explanation.surface: Word has it that some washed-up, misled hero has become utterly ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: "I'm told" looks like a sound-alike signal, but it is just fodder: its letters make up the fodder along with HERO FADED.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle-of-the-road means unadventurous and ordinary, so unremarkable.

clue.text: Time involving checks of wild animals following death (7)

indicators.note: the animals come after death in the entry

blocks.note: death is the end
game is wild animals hunted for sport or food

explanation.surface: A time of inspecting wild animals after one has died.
explanation.walkthrough: Checks here are chess checks, not inspections: the endgame is the last phase of a chess game, when kings are hunted down.
explanation.definitionFit: The endgame is the final stage of chess, a time full of checks on the king.

clue.text: Musical effect always featuring in R&B (6)

indicators.note: always appears inside R&B

blocks.note: R&B written without the ampersand
ever means always, as in ever-ready

explanation.surface: Some sound effect is a constant presence in rhythm and blues records.
explanation.walkthrough: R&B is rhythm and blues; here it simply supplies its two letters around EVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverb, short for reverberation, is an echo effect added to music.

clue.text: Decline to enter a newly-written, amicable agreement (7,8)

indicators.note: the letters are written out anew in a different order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, fifteen letters

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to sign up to a freshly drafted friendly pact.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a refusal to sign, the opposite of the answer; the Entente Cordiale was the 1904 Anglo-French understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Entente cordiale is French for a friendly understanding between nations.

clue.text: Changed wheels before getting to another place (9)

indicators.note: the letters of wheels are changed around
the rearranged wheels come ahead of the second piece

blocks.note: anagram of WHEELS
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A driver swaps the wheels before setting off for somewhere new.
explanation.walkthrough: "before" does double duty in feel but only once in fact: it is the fodder for ERE, and the order is simply left to right.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain adverb of direction: heading somewhere other than here is going to another place.

clue.text: All the best extras? (3-3)

definitions.note: "extras" is plural: two byes written together

blocks.note: a parting wish, said when taking leave
in cricket a bye is a run counted as an extra; the plural means two side by side

explanation.surface: A sign-off wishing the finest of the supporting cast well.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run scored when the ball passes the batsman untouched, counted as an extra; the question mark covers pairing two of them.
explanation.definitionFit: "All the best" is said on parting, just like bye-bye.

clue.text: Walked a mile, then ran (6)

indicators.note: the second piece comes next

blocks.note: used as it stands
m is the abbreviation for mile
dye that runs has bled

explanation.surface: Someone strolled a mile, then broke into a run.
explanation.walkthrough: "ran" wants to mean moved fast, contradicting walked; it is ran as colours do in the wash, which is bled.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a leisurely pace.

clue.text: Within a couple of minutes, one senior journo acted dumb (5)

indicators.note: one sits inside the two minutes

blocks.note: two Ms, m being minute
Roman numeral one
an editor, the senior journalist, abbreviated

explanation.surface: A top journalist stays silent for a minute or two.
explanation.walkthrough: Dumb here means without speech, not stupid: to mime is to act without words.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimed means acted out without speaking, which is acting dumb.

clue.text: Relinquish valuable item, mostly for drink (9)

indicators.note: most of the word, with its last letter dropped

blocks.note: to demit is to resign or give up an office
ASSET without its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone sells off a treasured possession to pay for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: DEMIT is a rare, formal word for giving up a post; the rest is ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: A demitasse is a small cup of strong black coffee, so a drink.

clue.text: Buzz in the neighbourhood? (5,4)

blocks.note: the surface pushes a stir of excitement; the setter means a phone call, as in give me a buzz
the surface pushes an area abuzz; the setter means a call to a nearby number

explanation.surface: Excitement or gossip going round the area.
explanation.walkthrough: Buzz reads as a local stir of excitement, but "give me a buzz" means phone me.
explanation.definitionFit: A local call is a phone call to a nearby number, a buzz in the neighbourhood.

clue.text: A lack of established routine in your dreams (2,3)

blocks.note: a way can mean an established method or habit; here there is none
both are scornful refusals

explanation.surface: Your dreams have no set pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes "in your dreams" literal; it is the retort meaning that will never happen.
explanation.definitionFit: "In your dreams!" and "No way!" both flatly reject a hope.

clue.text: Offensive racket outside room periodically (7)

indicators.note: the racket goes round the other letters
take letters at regular intervals: the second and fourth of room

blocks.note: a racket is a din
r O o M, every other letter

explanation.surface: An objectionable din is coming from outside the room now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Noisome looks like it should mean noisy, which the racket encourages, but it means offensive, especially of smells.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means disgusting or offensive, typically of a smell.

clue.text: Explain the meaning of painter prettifying frames (9)

indicators.note: the words frame the answer, holding it inside them

blocks.note: runs from the third letter of painter into the start of prettifying

explanation.surface: A critic explains what a painter is up to in making pretty frames.
explanation.walkthrough: Frames fits the painting picture so well it looks like the object, not the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: construing what something means, as a critic does with a painting.

clue.text: Shortage holding physical education back to intensify (6)

indicators.note: the reversed shortage holds PE inside it
the shortage is turned back to front

blocks.note: NEED turned back
the standard abbreviation for school sport

explanation.surface: Cutting back on school sport only makes a problem worse.
explanation.walkthrough: Back could apply to PE too, but EP inside NEED read backwards gives DEPEEN; only the need is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To deepen is to make or become more intense.

clue.text: Vessel bearing King’s flag (8)

indicators.note: the vessel carries the king inside it

blocks.note: a steamer is a steamship
R for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A ship flies the monarch's banner.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s is not possessive: it stands for "is", linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow flag or pennant.

clue.text: You start to stagger after immediately standing (6)

indicators.note: take the first letter of stagger
the you-and-S pair comes after STAT

blocks.note: stat, from Latin statim, is medical shorthand for at once
text-speak spelling of you
first letter of stagger

explanation.surface: Having got to your feet at once, you begin to totter.
explanation.walkthrough: Standing means rank here, not being upright, though the surface is all about getting up.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is one's standing or position in society.

clue.text: Cushion sags at the back again and again (6)

indicators.note: take the last letter of sags

blocks.note: last letter of sags
often means repeatedly

explanation.surface: A cushion keeps sinking at the rear, time after time.
explanation.walkthrough: Cushion looks like a noun in a sagging sofa; it is the verb, to lessen the blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Cushion is the verb, to lessen the force of a blow, and making a blow gentler is exactly this.

clue.text: Boycott maybe in favour of lengthy cricket match (7)

blocks.note: pro means for
a Test match lasts up to five days

explanation.surface: Geoffrey Boycott, perhaps, favours a long cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Boycott was a famous England batsman, which makes the cricket surface seamless; the capital hides a boycott, a kind of protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: refusing to deal with someone is one kind of organised objection, hence "maybe".

clue.text: Type of coffee, according to hearsay, that can stimulate desire (7)

indicators.note: what is heard, not what is written

blocks.note: filter coffee is brewed by dripping through paper; the potion word sounds identical

explanation.surface: Rumour says a certain coffee works as an aphrodisiac.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase rather than a single word: a philtre is a love potion.
explanation.definitionFit: A philtre is a magic potion meant to arouse love or desire.

clue.text: Silence a fan of religion (6)

blocks.note: sh is the call for silence
if you are into something you are a fan of it

explanation.surface: Quieting someone who is keen on religion.
explanation.walkthrough: "of" links the wordplay to the definition, though it reads as part of "a fan of".
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is the indigenous faith of Japan, one religion among many.

clue.text: Pack from stockpile picked up (5)

indicators.note: caught by the ear, as a radio picks up a signal

blocks.note: a hoard is a stockpile; the crowd word sounds identical

explanation.surface: A packet is taken from a store of supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: Pack reads as a verb or a packet next to stockpile; it is the noun, a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Pack as a noun for a large unruly crowd of people or animals.

clue.text: Donut cried out to be covered in fudge (9)

indicators.note: cried is knocked out of shape
the rearranged letters sit inside fudge

blocks.note: to fudge is to fake
anagram of CRIED

explanation.surface: A doughnut wails at being smothered in fudge.
explanation.walkthrough: Fudge sits naturally with a donut as a topping; it is the verb, to fake. A friedcake is American for a doughnut.
explanation.definitionFit: A friedcake is a small cake fried in fat, such as a doughnut.

clue.text: Sour berries primarily found beneath tree (5)

indicators.note: take the first letter of berries
in a down entry, the B sits under the tree

blocks.note: acer is the maple genus
first letter of berries

explanation.surface: Bitter berries lie on the ground below a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Acerb is a rare form of acerbic.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb means sour or bitter in taste.

clue.text: Extremely strict director enters animal refuge (9)

indicators.note: the director goes into the refuge

blocks.note: a nest is where an animal shelters
an arrow directs you where to go

explanation.surface: A very severe film director walks into an animal sanctuary.
explanation.walkthrough: Director suggests a film-maker or boss; it is a signpost arrow. Extremely here marks the superlative.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow can mean strict or limited, and narrowest is the extreme of that.

clue.text: Elite players had a mare at the outset (1-4)

indicators.note: take the first letter of mare

blocks.note: had a meal, ate
used as it stands
first letter of mare

explanation.surface: The top squad had a nightmare right from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: "had a mare" is British slang for having a disastrous time, which suits a sports team; split it as ATE + A + M.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporting idiom: a club's first-choice side, its best players.

clue.text: Do cats roam in smallish groups? (6)

indicators.note: the letters wander into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, six letters

explanation.surface: A question about whether cats wander in little gangs.
explanation.walkthrough: An octad is a group of eight, small enough to call smallish.
explanation.definitionFit: Octads are sets of eight, which are smallish groups.

clue.text: Don’t forget about any plant in a group (8)

blocks.note: re means about, concerning
any plant belonging to a group is a member of it

explanation.surface: A reminder to include every plant in a garden bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The member is cryptically described: any plant in a botanical group is one of its members.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym put negatively: an instruction not to forget is one to keep something in mind.
